prompt.title: PostgreSQL slow-query diagnosis and tuning from plan evidence

var.name: query
var.example: SELECT ... FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON ... WHERE o.store_id = $1 AND o.created_at >= $2 ORDER BY o.created_at DESC LIMIT 50

variables.var: the statement as the application sends it, with parameter types

var.name: plan_digest
var.example: (output of explain_plan_triage.py on EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON))

variables.var: the pre-digested plan, not the raw JSON

var.name: schema_facts
var.example: orders 48M rows; indexes: pk(id), (customer_id); store_id has 1,200 distinct values; autovacuum last analyze 9 days ago

variables.var: the latency target for this query

context.platform: PostgreSQL 17; Flyway 12.4.0 migrations; the application uses prepared statements through the JDBC driver 42.7.14.

instructions.step: State the bottleneck in one sentence, citing the plan node and its numbers (actual time, rows, loops, buffers).
For every scan and join in the digest, compare estimated with actual rows; a ratio beyond 10x in either direction is a statistics problem to fix before any index.
Propose at most three changes, ranked by expected effect, each with the predicate or ordering it serves, its write and storage cost, and the measurement that would confirm it.

Write each schema change as a Flyway migration that builds indexes with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction, and each query rewrite with an argument that it returns the same rows, NULLs and duplicates included.
Say how to re-measure with the same parameter values, and whether the prepared statement may switch to a generic plan after five executions (plan_cache_mode).

invariants.inv: Every claim cites a plan node and a number from the digest; nothing is inferred from the query text alone.
Misestimates beyond 10x are addressed (ANALYZE, extended statistics, or a statistics target) before an index is proposed for that node.
Each proposed index names the exact predicate and sort it serves and its cost on writes.
Indexes on live tables are created CONCURRENTLY in a non-transactional migration.
Each rewrite is shown to be semantically equivalent.

anti_goals.no: No index for every column in the WHERE clause.
No configuration changes (work_mem, random_page_cost) as the first fix, and never globally for one query.
No query hints or extensions the platform does not have.

output_contract.file: diagnosis note: bottleneck, misestimates, ranked changes, measurements
non-transactional migration for any new index
output_contract.report: A table of plan nodes cited (node, metric, value), then the ranked changes with expected and measured effect.

verification.check: Every sentence in the diagnosis that names a cost has a node reference from the digest.
The digest's misestimate list is empty after the statistics fix, or each remaining item is explained.
Each index line in the migration has a comment naming the predicate and sort.
The migration contains CONCURRENTLY and runs outside a transaction.
An equivalence test runs old and new query on the Testcontainers database and compares results.

prompt.task: Diagnose why this query misses {{slo}} and propose the smallest safe changes that meet it, following every invariant.
